title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration & Escalation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates our customer-success and support processes for enterprise customers: onboarding, technical integration, known issues and workarounds, escalation flows, routine health checks, and QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers (L1/L2/L3), and SRE/Platform on-call.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers
- Solutions Engineers / Integration Engineers
- Support (L1/L2/L3) and SREs
- Account Executives and Partner Ops for commercial coordination

Objectives
- Reduce time to production for enterprise integrations to <= 10 business days for standard integrations.
- Provide deterministic escalation timelines and owner handoffs.
- Capture recurring known issues and workarounds to shorten TSAT-impacting incidents.
- Standardize health-check metrics and QBR templates for consistent customer reviews.

Service SLOs (for context)
- API availability: 99.95% monthly for Redwood API (hosted).
- Critical incident response: initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes (PagerDuty).
- High-severity incident mitigation: 4-hour recovery target for customer-facing degradations.

Ownership and Contacts
- Primary owner: customer-success (CS Ops)
- Technical owner: eng-platform (onboarding infra)
- Escalation contact: support-oncall@redwood.ai (PagerDuty 24x7)
- Enterprise AM: Account-specific (populate in customer record)
- Slack channels: #cs-enterprise, #support-oncall, #se-implementations

Onboarding Checklist (high-level)
1) Commercial handoff
   - Confirm contract details, seat counts, dedicated capacity or hosted tier, data residency and compliance needs.
   - Owner: Account Executive -> CSM.
2) Kickoff meeting (Day 0)
   - Attendees: CSM, SE, customer technical lead, PM/PO, legal if required.
   - Outcomes: project milestones, integration owner, IP/keys process, target go-live date.
3) Access and security (Day 0-2)
   - Create API key scoped to customer (token rotation plan).
   - Confirm network allowlists and VPC/Private deployment requirements.
   - If Private deployment: schedule on-prem packaging and credential exchange.
   - Owner: SE and customer security contact.
4) Integration and test (Day 1-7)
   - Integration checklist (see below).
   - Run smoke tests and validation scenarios.
   - Owner: SE / Customer engineer.
5) Performance and SLO validation (Day 3-10)
   - Run perf harness for typical workload: latency p95, p99, and throughput targets.
   - Validate cost/per-token estimates.
6) Production cutover (Day 7-14)
   - Canary rollout plan, rollback steps, and monitoring alerts configured in Redwood Console.
   - Owner: CSM + SE + SRE for first 72h monitoring.

Integration Guide (core items)
- API endpoints: use the customer-specific host or the global hosted endpoint.
- Authentication: API keys via Authorization header. Example curl: 
  curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Hello"}'

- Network requirements:
  - Outbound TLS to api.redwood.ai:443
  - If using Dedicated or Private: provide IP ranges for allowlist and peering details.

- Deployment modes and notes:
  - Hosted: simplest; ensure API key and quotas are set.
  - Dedicated: reserved GPU pools; schedule capacity provisioning window (2-5 business days).
  - Private: requires installation window and cert/KMS exchange.

- Sample validation test cases:
  1) Authentication test: call health endpoint and confirm HTTP 200 and account id match.
  2) Latency test: 100 requests at target prompt size; measure p95 < customer SLA.
  3) Functional test: assert semantic correctness for a canonical prompt set.

Checklist Table (integration requirements)
| Item | Requirement | Owner | Target completion |
|-------|-------------|-------|------------------|
| API key | Scoped key created, stored in vault | SE | Day 1 |
| Allowlist | IPs or VPC peering confirmed | Customer + SE | Day 2 |
| Smoke tests | Pass 10 canonical prompts | SE + Customer | Day 3 |
| Monitoring | Alerts for 5xx rate, latency p95 | SRE + CSM | Before cutover |

Escalation Playbook
Purpose: provide a clear, time-bound path for customer-impacting issues so SLAs and expectations remain aligned.

Severity definitions and SLA expectations:
- Sev 1 (Critical): production outage or total data loss affecting customer business.
  - Initial ack: 15 minutes (PagerDuty).
  - Assignment: within 30 minutes.
  - Target mitigation: 4 hours.
  - Communication cadence: hourly until mitigation.
- Sev 2 (High): significant degradation impacting many users or core functionality.
  - Initial ack: 1 hour.
  - Assignment: within 4 hours.
  - Target mitigation: 24 hours.
  - Communication cadence: every 4-8 hours.
- Sev 3 (Medium): partial impact, workaround exists, not blocking major flows.
  - Initial ack: 8 business hours.
  - Mitigation target: 3-7 days.
- Sev 4 (Low): minor issue, feature request, or improvement.
  - Handled in standard support queue (next sprint).

Escalation path (ordered):
1) L1 Support (CS Support team): triage, reproduce, attempt documented workaround. Owner: L1.
2) L2 Support (Product Support / SE): deeper diagnostics, collect logs, attach to ticket. Owner: L2.
3) L3 (SRE / Eng Serving Runtime): code fixes, infra changes, deploy rollback. Owner: L3 with eng owner assigned.
4) Executive escalation: invoked for multi-day outages or contractual SLA breaches; involve CSM Director, VP Eng, and Legal as needed.

PagerDuty and Slack workflow:
- PagerDuty on-call receives alerts for Sev1/2. Use runbook pinned in PagerDuty incident.
- Create a JIRA incident ticket: project = CS-INC, link to PagerDuty incident, tag customer id.
- Post status updates to #cs-enterprise and customer-facing status page if external customer update required.

Triage checklist (L1)
- Reproduce the issue with customer-provided input.
- Collect request_id, timestamps, and logs (include request headers with redaction).
- Check recent deploys and config changes in Redwood Console.
- Validate quotas and limits (rate limit, dedicated capacity).
- If workaround exists, present to customer and schedule permanent fix.

Known Issues and Workarounds
Note: this section is continuously updated; add entries to related_pages and label with issue-id.

| ID | Symptom | Root Cause (summary) | Workaround | Owner |
|-----|---------|----------------------|-----------|-------|
| KI-2025-001 | Repeated 429s for burst batch jobs | Default rate limiter not tuned for bursty workloads | Request L2 to increase burst window or enable client-side exponential backoff (jitter) | eng-platform |
| KI-2025-007 | Tokenization differences vs. reference | Model tokenizer mismatch for legacy prompt format | Use canonical tokenizer CLI: redwood tokenizer normalize --input '...'; adjust prompt to new tokenization | applied-ml-and-evals |
| KI-2026-002 | Intermittent p99 latency spikes during peak | KV cache eviction and noisy neighbor on shared nodes | For Dedicated customers: enable node pinning or provision extra capacity; for Hosted: temporarily route to a compatible lower-latency model variant | eng-serving-runtime |

Support Process and Ticket Lifecycle
- Channels accepted: Support portal (preferred), support@redwood.ai, and customer-designated Slack channel for high-touch accounts.
- Ticket fields required: customer_id, environment (prod/staging), severity, reproducible steps, sample input, expected vs actual.
- SLA targets: initial response per severity (see Escalation Playbook).
- Ownership rules: ticket moves to L2 after 8 business hours without resolution; L2 must update ticket with diagnostics and ETA.

Health Checks and QBR Materials
Recurring health-check cadence:
- Weekly check-in (CS + Customer technical lead): review alerts, any open Sev2/1 incidents, helper tasks.
- 30/60/90-day milestone reviews during onboarding.
- Monthly automated health report delivered to customer and CSM.

Health-check metrics (minimum)
- API success rate (5xx rate and 4xx rate)
- Latency p50/p95/p99 for representative prompt sizes
- Request volume and tokens consumed (daily and rolling 30d)
- Error budgets and SLO burn rate
- Model quality regressions flagged by eval harness (APPLIED-ML scores)

QBR template (CS-led)
1) Executive summary: usage growth, health, risks and opportunities.
2) Metrics deep dive: adoption by team, top routes, latency and cost trends.
3) Incidents and RCA summary since last QBR.
4) Roadmap & upcoming changes: planned model upgrades, infra maintenance windows.
5) Action items and owners.

Example QBR agenda (60 minutes):
- 0-10m: Exec summary and wins
- 10-25m: Metrics and usage patterns
- 25-40m: Incidents and mitigation actions
- 40-55m: Roadmap discussion and feature asks
- 55-60m: Next steps and action owners

Templates and Artifacts to attach to QBR
- Monthly health report (CSV & dashboard link)
- Incident timeline document for Sev1/2 events
- Integration checklist sign-off

Appendix A: Example runbook snippets
- Check recent errors for customer via CLI:
  redwood logs query --customer-id CUST-123 --from '2026-02-01T00:00:00Z' --to '2026-02-10T00:00:00Z' --filter 'level>=ERROR'

- Repro command for API call (curl):
  curl -s -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Summarize the following text"}' | jq '.'

Appendix B: Webhook / Callback config (example)
- Example payload (use customer webhook to receive async outputs):
  endpoint: https://customer.example.com/redwood/callback
  headers: 'X-Redwood-Signature' for verification, 'Content-Type: application/json'
  sample body (POST): '{
    'job_id': 'JOB-abc123',
    'status': 'complete',
    'result_url': 'https://storage.redwood.ai/results/JOB-abc123'
  }'

How to update this document
- Owners must review this playbook quarterly. Add new known issues as they are triaged and include the issue-id prefix KI-YYYY-NNN in the labels.
- For procedural changes (escalation SLA updates, new PagerDuty rotations), notify owners and update related_pages with new runbooks.

Related pages and resources

- Engineering runbooks: incident response and deployment rollback
